analysis.title: Daily Points, November 6, 2026
key_insights: US equities are stabilizing ahead of the jobs reports after a global selloff. US futures are up 0.25% (S&P) to 1.5% (Nasdaq) after the indices fell 4-5% the prior day. TSX futures are slightly lower.

Asia-Pacific followed the US lower. Tokyo fell about 6% and Seoul's Kospi lost 6% after circuit breakers were tripped. Chinese indices fell 1-2%. Taiwan lost almost 5% and the government imposed a short selling limit. European cash markets were down 1-2%.

Sovereign bonds are not attracting much flow. Gilts are mildly selling off after the BoE, US Treasuries are slightly cheaper, and euro-area government bonds have a slight richening bias. Most major currencies are slightly weaker against the USD.
October US nonfarm payrolls are released at 8:30am ET. Scotiabank pencils in +100k, versus a 65k consensus and 29k prior. Unemployment is expected at 4.2%.
October Canadian jobs are released at 8:30am ET. Scotiabank forecasts +15k, in line with consensus of 15k, after -68.3k prior. The unemployment rate is expected at 6.5%.

The Canadian federal budget adds under 0.25% to 2027 GDP growth by Scotiabank's first-pass estimate, and probably considerably less. New measures total about $15B in FY27 and $34B in 2028 relative to the Spring update.

The budget adds confidence to Scotiabank's forecast of three more BoC rate hikes, with ongoing risk of more, and raises expectations for a December hike. The BoC will not fully incorporate the budget until the January MPR.

Ottawa projects a peak deficit of $65B this year, falling to about $53B in five years. Scotiabank expects deficit projections to be raised and pushed out, citing serially ambitious forecasts, execution risk, likely cost overruns and repeated added measures. It says debt issuance numbers should be treated with caution.

The budget relies on a commodity dividend and positive terms-of-trade shock from high oil. If oil fell sharply the dividend would reverse, because the government has assumed it continues for years and pre-spent it.

Total new spending of $152B versus the Spring update is paid for by $158B of higher revenues and lower expenses. Ottawa expects about C$24B a year of extra revenue and about $12B a year of direct program spending cuts, including EDC/BDC job cuts.

The foreign home buyer ban is relaxed, which Scotiabank says could bring back some condo demand in struggling markets such as Toronto and Vancouver. The fuel excise tax cut is extended to March, which Scotiabank calls bad policy and a multi-billion-dollar gift to refiners.

The updated five-year BoC Monetary Policy Framework drops references to fully inclusive maximum employment and climate change. It states that price stability is the best way to achieve maximum sustainable employment and growth.

Financial sector measures in the budget: mid-sized banks must become widely held at $25B in equity, up from $12B. OSFI gets a secondary competition objective. Deposit insurance rises to $250,000. BDC and EDC are consolidated. An RRSP-for-life replaces the RRIF/annuity conversion at 71. The C$25B Canada Strong Fund is a sovereign wealth fund that Scotiabank views skeptically.

Scotiabank lists several possible causes for the AI and tech selloff after the US midterms: policy risk for data centres, legislative gridlock with Trump saying he will veto Democratic bills, a long-overdue valuation correction, pending payrolls and next week's CPI that inform the December FOMC, and risk of escalation in the war with Iran.
Chilean October CPI was 4.5% y/y versus 4.6% consensus and 4.1% prior. It reinforces the hawkish tone of the BCCh minutes.

Market snapshot: S&P 500 -4.4% on the day and -5.9% over one month. Nasdaq -5.5% and -11.9%. Dow -3.4%. Nikkei -6.0% and -18.7% over one month. S&P/TSX -2.0%. WTI +0.6%. Gold -0.5%. Silver +0.6% on the day and -15.0% over one month.

sector_views.rationale: The selloff is attributed to US legislative and policy risk for data centres, valuation concerns and macro event risk. The report says data centres should absorb more of their related costs.
The budget raises the widely-held threshold for mid-sized banks, adds a competition objective for OSFI and raises deposit insurance to $250,000. The report says further research is needed.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Scotiabank's forecast is well above the 65k consensus, and 29k was the prior reading.
Consensus is below Scotiabank's forecast. The print informs the December FOMC.
Unchanged from the prior reading of 4.2%.
The prior readings were 0.1% m/m and 3.0% y/y.
A rebound from -68.3k is expected. It bears on the BoC's expected hikes.
Unchanged from the prior reading of 6.5%.
Slightly below the 4.6% consensus and above the 4.1% prior. It reinforces the hawkish BCCh minutes.
The prior reading was 48.0. It is released at 10am ET after payrolls.
The next meeting is December 9. Scotiabank forecasts three more hikes.
The next FOMC meeting is December 9, 2026.

risk_factors: Escalation of the war with Iran.
Payrolls on Friday and next week's US CPI could shift expectations for the December FOMC.
A long-overdue equity valuation correction in AI and tech.
A sharp fall in oil would reverse Canada's commodity dividend and force fiscal tightening.
Canadian deficit projections and debt issuance numbers carry execution and cost-overrun risk.
US policy gridlock and legislation targeting data centre costs.
charts_described: Chart 13 shows the refining margin offsetting the federal fuel tax suspension, in cents per litre on a weekly average.
vol_and_positioning: Circuit breakers were tripped in Seoul's Kospi, and Taiwan imposed a short selling limit after the Asian selloff.
The Nasdaq is down 11.9% over one month and the Nikkei is down 18.7%, per the market table.
geopolitical: Risk of escalation in the war with Iran after Trump said a decision on what to do next was coming soon.
US midterm election results and policy gridlock, with Trump saying he will veto anything the Democrats offer.
US legislative actions aimed at data centres, including the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340), the POWER Up Act and Senator Cotton's DATA Act.

tension_points.bull_case: Futures are rebounding by 0.25% to 1.5% ahead of payrolls, and the selloff may be a long overdue valuation correction rather than a fundamental break.
tension_points.bear_case: US data centre legislation, midterm gridlock, Iran escalation risk and a hot payrolls or CPI print could push the FOMC toward further tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Payrolls on Friday and next week's US CPI, which inform how the FOMC acts in December.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher oil and positive terms of trade improve fiscal balances and fund the budget's investment focus.
tension_points.bear_case: Much lower oil would reverse the dividend, because the government has assumed it continues for years and pre-spent it.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sharp fall in oil prices.
